title: Ethiopian Chicken with Vegetables
community: Urban Ethiopia — the one-pot family chicken meal
author: Mama Tigist
desc: Ethiopian Chicken and Vegetables — chicken pieces simmered in a mild Ethiopian spice sauce with potatoes, carrots, and tomatoes. The balanced family meal — Ethiopian spices applied to the classic chicken-and-vegetable one-pot, suitable for children and those preferring mild food.
longDesc: Doro ke-Atkilit is the family-friendly chicken dish — the Ethiopian spice tradition applied to a mild, vegetable-rich stew that everyone at the table can enjoy. Less ceremonial than Doro Wat, more practical for everyday family meals.
steps: Cook onions until golden. Add garlic, ginger, turmeric, berbere, tomatoes.
Return chicken. Add water. Simmer covered 30 minutes.
Add potatoes and carrots. Simmer 20 more minutes.
Vegetables should be tender; chicken falling-tender.
chefTips: Add potatoes and carrots after the chicken has been cooking 30 minutes.
Very light berbere — this is intentionally mild for family eating.
cookingScience: See ETH038 for chicken-and-vegetable stew science.
sustainabilityTips: Extending chicken with vegetables — more nutritious and economical.
servedWith: As a standalone meal for children
culturalNote: Doro ke-Atkilit is the Ethiopian family dinner — the dish that includes everyone at the table, from the youngest child to the eldest. Ethiopian cooking's remarkable capacity to be both ceremonially significant (Doro Wat) and practically family-friendly (this dish) is one of its greatest strengths.
